summary: 40-foot pole lookout in the Okanogan NF built 1934, shortened to 10 feet in 1954 for training, gone after 1963; a trip report shows two footings.

facts.design: 40-foot pole tower with an L-5 cab; shortened to 10 feet in 1954 and used to train lookouts
facts.status_note: Tower removed or burned in 1963; a trip report shows footings

visit.trail_note: Trail from Lost Lake, just under a mile each way with about 650 feet of climb; a road crosses the trail at 4,100 feet, where roadside parking is possible.

events.note: 40-foot pole tower with an L-5 cab; a 1934 newspaper report describes a road to it

Registered November 23, 2012 as US 1470, WA 370; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts page says Colville National Forest. The register, firelookout.com and the trip report say Okanogan National Forest. The story uses Okanogan.
The register says removed; firelookout.com and the trip report say destroyed or burned. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Several search results describe a different Strawberry Mountain lookout (a 54-foot derrick tower built 1936 near 48.45 N, 118.94 W) and a Skamania County Strawberry Mountain. Neither is used. The brief has no height; 12.2 m comes from the register's 40-foot pole tower. The access level is left out because the trip report gives trail directions and mentions no closure but cites no official rule. The 'Two footings' captions in the trip report carry no date. The brief's access 'unknown' is unchanged.
